utterances.text: Here, on the hand, is the number, and now we are checking the number on the hand and comparing it to the list, to the HVO list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You can continue. Thank you. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a number that was found on the body, that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that some of the bodies were charred. Is that an example?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's the charred body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see the piece of paper there pretty clearly, can you not?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a charred body too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what does this show?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: The bodies are taken away to the grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, again, placed in the order that corresponds to your list, which is Exhibit 307?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is happening here?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: This is a religious ritual, the bowing at a burial, during a burial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the congregation to participate in that service came from?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: These are people from Stari Vitez, inhabitants of Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can hear the sound of machinery in the background. What's happening that we don't see here?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Now the excavator is digging another grave. Because the first one was too small to take all the bodies, a second one is being dug now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there some sense of urgency to get the job done at this point?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is getting dark, and we couldn't wait for the first grave to be finished and to start the second one. Because it was getting dark, we had to hurry up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also losing people, people leaving?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mirjan Kupreskic asks to be excused to go out. He says he's not feeling well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. All right. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Is it permissible to proceed without --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. With the consent -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I think we will proceed with the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last question was whether people had been leaving throughout the day. Was that a problem?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were they leaving and what was happening?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: It was getting dark and shots were -- firing was heard. Some shots were coming. And for this reason, the number of people was reduced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the stench a problem as well for some people?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. People couldn't stand it anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is happening now?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Well, as it is getting dark, we could not unload them to the meadow. We simply drove the truck to the grave, and from there on, we buried them directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this would be the second grave then, the one that we heard being dug earlier?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's happening here?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Well, here again we are verifying the -- checking the number that we have on the record, on the list, and the number which is attached to the bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you. If the witness could now be shown previously admitted Exhibit 294?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does this show, Mr. Rehibic?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: These are the graves where the bodies were buried in two rows. These wooden sticks in both rows, this is the first row and the numbers from left to right, one, two, three, four, and this is the second row, also from left to right in ascending order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If the witness may be shown the next photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 310.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Exhibit 310 has been placed on the ELMO, which is a photograph. What is that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: This -- here we see what this grave site looks like today where all those bodies were buried. Along this fence we have the first row and up there is the second one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the sticks that were placed there five years ago are still, for the most part, there; is that right, the markers?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, they're still there, unchanged. As we put them then, nothing has changed to this day, although some changes have been made, but we need more verifications and authentication and so forth to really change anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a memorial plaque at the cemetary to indicate who is buried there?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: There is a memorial plaque at the cemetery with names of the victims according to the record made by the commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: May the witness be shown the next photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 311.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Do you mind, Mr. Moskowitz, if I ask a question to the witness since we are still on Exhibit 310? I wonder whether those houses are all Muslim or are there Croats -- I mean, the houses we see here in this photograph. Are they Muslim or Croat? Are there also Croatian houses?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: These houses we see here are Muslim, and behind them there is the Lasic (phoen) Street where there are also some Croat houses and there were several families there with us. For the duration of the war, they were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: This house, the first one we see, the big one with a two-sloped roof, is a Muslim house?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: As well as the other one to the right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what Exhibit 311 shows?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Well, here we see this plaque which is there today with the names of the victims according to the list that was done, that is, the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The actual list that's located inside the showcase or the case, do you know what that is made out of and whether it is disintegrating or whether it is still in existence?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: It's still in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Finally, may the witness be shown the last photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 312.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us now what 312 is, Exhibit 312?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Here we see the list of those buried into graves in the order of the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I placed some little dots next to certain names on that list. Can you see them, those little dots?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Starting at the top, and it may be difficult for you to read, but right at the top, looking at number 6 on that list --

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: More, more, more. I can't see. I can't see anything. I can't see it. You have to move it away ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: You have to pull it back a little bit. That's better for now. And pull it down a little bit so we can see it at the very top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The first dot -- the picture is not very good -- but that should be number 6. Can you read that name? That's better, much better.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Sukrija Ahmic from Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And look at number 8. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Number 8 is Meho (Vehbija) Hrustanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Skipping down to number 13?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Number 13 is Pezer Aziz from Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 14?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Number 14, Sabahudin Zec from Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 15?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Number 15, Rasim (Ramiza) Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We didn't put a dot next to 16, but please read his name out as well.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Number 16, Nazif (Ramiza) Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Seventeen?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Ramiz (Seho) Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 18?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Eighteen is NN, a male.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you since identified who that unknown male is, number 18? You may refer to your list if you need to.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: We've already said here in the records that we supplemented it; 18 is Musafer Puscul.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is 21?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Twenty-one is Fahrudin (Hasima) Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the name in the parenthesis between Ahmic and Fahrudin, what does that signify?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Between the brackets, it's the name of the father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the father of Fahrudin is a man by the name of Hasim; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If we can now look down and move the exhibit to show numbers 95 through 98, and push it down -- yes, a little more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do we have there? Number 95 first.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Ninety-five is Naser (Sakib) Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 96?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Edina Ahmic, Nasera Ahmic, and 98, I can't see exactly, but again Naser Ahmic. That was when we took over the bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 98 is unfortunately cut off on this photograph, but if you could look at your list, could you tell me that person's name, number 98?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Ninety-eight is Sejo (Naser) Ahmic, a three-month-old child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more name I would like you to point out for us, if you can, and it's difficult. Number 38 on that list. If it could be moved so that we can see number 38? A little farther down. Right there. That's good.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Thirty-eight is Abdulah (Mehmed) Brko from Visegrad, brought under number 23 of the HVO record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see it on the list at the cemetery now placed in front of you on the TV screen, number 38?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thirty-eight says Abdulah (Mehmed) Brko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the bodies you received that day from Ahmici or were they from other areas as well?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Not all were from Ahmici but an overwhelming majority of them were. There were also bodies from the area of Gacice, the area of Vitez, that is from Kolonija, Stari Vitez, Rijeka, Donja Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many bodies did you calculate were from Ahmici and, of course, understanding that many of the bodies could not be identified either as to name or as to place, but to the best that you could figure, how many bodies that you received that day were from Ahmici or from the immediate area of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: An overwhelming majority, I should say, more than 70, more than 80 bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where other bodies from Ahmici were buried?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether all the bodies were found in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No, I do not know that either because -- because of the operations with the HVO, I was in Stari Vitez all the time, so that I had no information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, this ends this portion of his testimony. I have one area I would like to get into that will take maybe five, ten minutes, although it may be best to do that after lunch because we are already over the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. All right. We adjourn now until 2.15. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.40 p.m. 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Mirjan Kupreskic, are you better?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I'm feeling better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Moskowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour, on reconsideration, although I do tender at this moment the Exhibits 305, 306, 307, 308, 309, 310, 311, and 312.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. But on 307A, I noticed that there's an inconsistency with the original in Bosniak. The date is 10th of March whereas in the original it is, I think, 18th of March. I can see. I mean, I think -- so which -- the 18th of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: The exhibit in front of the witness is dated -- and perhaps we can ask the witness to give us the date of the actual exhibit in front of you? That would be 307, if that is the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 307, yes. 307A is the 10th of March which I think is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I think the translation was taken from a different version of this exhibit, and so that is the difference -- or explains the difference in the dates. Let me ask: Does the witness have Exhibit 307 in front of him now? Yes. And what is the date on that exhibit on that list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 18th of March, 1994. The 18th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And it's my understanding that the translation we have is identical with the exception of the date and a couple of instances where he updated the list of dead persons, but I propose, and perhaps it is a good idea, to submit this Exhibit 307 for another translation so that we can be assured that we have exactly what's on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. And also in the translation we don't have the -- I mean, there are two signatures at the end. We don't know who signed. Probably one of them was the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I can ask. I think I know who signed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you tell us who signed the list that you have in front of you, 307?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Under 1, Vatres Ramo, and under 2, Dzidic Ehes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who are these two people?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: They were from my team, from the team who was with me at the burial and in the carrying out of this task. They are members of the army, of the criminal -- they are criminal technicians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were, in fact -- at least one of them was on that videotape making a list of names, you could see him writing on a piece of paper; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Under 1, Vatric Samo. He conducted -- he was the head of the commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, with the permission of the Court, if I might? Can you explain how it came about that the burial took place in April of '93 and the list was not dated until '94?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I was about to put the same question.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: When we were working on the burial, Stari Vitez was under blockade, and we had the notes composed by the commission. After liberation, we established contact with the corps and then we did this on the 18th of April, but I left Vitez in April that year. But this is obviously a mistake, a typing error. It is a typing error. Have I been clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's your recollection that this was typed in April of '93, the 18th of April of '93; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: It can't be in April 1993. This -- this document can't have been written then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So maybe I did not follow your explanation. Could you explain it again? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: This was done after the cease-fire, on the basis of the evidence on the day of the burial because for the needs of the corps, we had to send them the data. Stari Vitez was under blockade, and we can't send the data, the documents, to the command of the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see if I understand what you're saying. The notes that you took at the burial, based on the HVO list, were made on April 28th, 1993, those notes, but those notes were not transcribed into this typewritten list until a later date, and that date is reflected on that list; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is so. Yes, yes. Because it was hand-written. Those notes were hand-written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you see those people on the videotape looking into the burial and writing on a piece of paper, those are the hand-written notes you're talking about; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those notes contain the positions of the bodies in the ground and were also based on the HVO list that you had with you that day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then those hand-written notes were then transcribed into this typewritten list that you have in front of you and which was signed by the two team members who were there?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Ranko Radovic and myself will question this witness. We have several questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I have shortened my questions because some of the questions I wanted to put have been put by the Prosecution. I'll follow my order. Cross-examined by Mr. Radovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said today that you retired as a member of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No. I was pensioned from the secretariat for internal affairs, from the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you gave the information to the investigator of the International Court, why did you say you were a teacher?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I am a teacher by profession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is your education, but your profession is a policeman. You were not retired from the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I was retired as the deputy secretary for Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However you take it, you are a member of the Ministry of the Interior, if not a policeman.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I was wearing -- I was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the moment when you made that statement, the testimony, were still active as a teacher?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because it says here that at the time, during the investigation, you were a teacher -- you were not a teacher?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: That is my profession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is your -- you can be a lawyer and work as a janitor.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: My profession now is a pensioner and I was a pensioner then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since April 1990, when you joined the headquarters of the Territorial Defence in Vitez, at the time when the headquarters was Bosnian and had a Bosnian and Croatian part, and then the Bosnians had their own headquarters. What was your job? What was your task?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I was the coordinator of units which were sent to the frontlines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you engage in collecting information, intelligence?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Every member of that unit gives information but not professionally, I didn't do it in the course of my job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said to the investigator that before 1993, I gathered information, collected intelligence, for our army. Every citizen has the duty -- that is our slogan, Civil Defence, et cetera, but I'm interested to know concretely whether your job was to gather information, intelligence. So that was the wrong statement. In your headquarters -- don't mention the name of the person -- was there a person who was the head of security?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the headquarters of the Territorial Defence, whose member you were too, the officer of security, did he give the information that dubious things are happening and that a lot of things can happen the next day?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: He didn't give that to me. That wasn't his duty. I said I was the coordinator in the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the -- from the 15th to the 16th of April, did you sleep in the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No, I slept in a private house. There was no room there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The security officer said that because of the danger that was threatening the town, all the members of the headquarters had to sleep in the premises of the headquarters. This didn't refer to you?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you conducted this sad job of burying the witnesses, why isn't your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Because on the 4th of April, 1994, I left for family reasons. I had to look after my young children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are the original documents which were testified to the authenticity of the signatures?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: They were with Vatres Ramo but I don't know what happened to them later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where could we get these documents now?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document that was sent to you by the HVO with the dead bodies, where could it be?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: It should be in the archives of the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you now some things connected -- relating to the persons on this list. But before that, I would like to hear why, in the introductory part of the record, it says that this is a list of the killed persons in the village of Ahmici, Veceriska, and Stari Vitez. But you mentioned two other places?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: In the list, we have Hercegovac, he is from Gacice, there are persons from Donja Veceriska, but in the preamble -- I don't know what the preamble says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you didn't participate in the writing of the document. Now we have to follow some kind of order. Let us see which persons were from Ahmici and which were not from Ahmici, in order to arrive at the figure of persons killed who were from Ahmici. I will not give you the names of the persons, I'll not mention the name. You will just comment whether the person is from Ahmici or not. I'll just give you the numbers from the list. Under number 11, there is an unknown older man, the body is charred. It doesn't say where his body was found. Do you know -- did you have any information from where he came, number 11 on this list?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: On this list, under number 11, it says unknown older man, charred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you know whether he is from Ahmici or not.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I want to tell you what data, what information I have. He was brought under list 94 of the HVO. The persons brought under that number were from Ahmici, Ahmic Vehbija is under 93 of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: If I may interrupt you? Sorry, counsel. I apologise, counsel Radovic. We have just realised that you are consulting a book. Could you explain to us what this book is, notebook or ... Because you're not reading from the list we received. We would like to know what sort of notebook this is.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: These are the notes made on the spot, on that day, my own notes, the notes I made during the burial, I copied from the HVO records the numbers without the data, without the description. Now I have all of these.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look now, the persons who wrote this list and who used your list, you said you didn't have it now, but you said who could have it. According to this list, you have number 11. Do you have any information or any data about whether the body is from Ahmici or from some other village?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I don't have this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 19. Follow the list. A similar situation. Tell me whether you have any knowledge about whether this body is from Ahmici or from somewhere else. Number 11 of this list.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: The record of the HVO says unknown, NN.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to know whether you have any information. You don't know about this person either. Then the same situation is with numbers 27 and 28 of the list. Probably the same situation. Can you tell us something about these numbers, these bodies?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I can say "Yes" or "No" but I feel the need to explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't object to that. I just wanted to simplify matters. I'm interested in knowing whether there is any information about whether these persons are from Ahmici or not. There is no doubt that they are the victims. We are not trying here for the whole Lasva Valley, but only for Ahmici. I would like to know whether you have information that these persons are from Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: If they are stated as unknown, we have no information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 32. We have the first and last name, but we don't know where the person comes from or came from.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Thirty-two, Siljak, Adem, we know that he lived in the Ahmici-Santici area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't know that. How do you know that he lived there? The name doesn't seem to fit Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: We have shorter last names too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thirty-three and 34. Again, two males, unknown.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: According to the information, the bodies that were brought from number 1 to 5, from numbers 1 to 5 of this list, we don't have the location --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't give me your notes. You have to link it to the numbers on this list. I'm asking about 33 and 34 on this list. We can't use the numbers from your notes. We don't have that notebook.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: The notebook doesn't matter. What matters is the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me about 33 and 34.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: If I had collected that information, I would tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now then, we have 35, Muhamed Neslanovic.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he from Ahmici or not?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes. Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the body came from Rovna. It states that he was wearing a camouflage uniform and trousers and in Croatian this is SNB, olive green, which is a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the trousers, but the olive green, that is a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Military socks were also found on the body. Did a part of the soldiers of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because there was a shortage of clothes, did they wear JNA clothes?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: The army didn't have enough clothes. These military uniforms, when the JNA disintegrated, when Slimenja was attacked, when the equipment was confiscated, many people took these uniforms on their own. This was robbery. This was looting. I don't think this is related.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we're at 36, Alic, Esref. Is he from Ahmici or some other village? I see a place near Zenica?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: He's from Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thirty-seven, unknown male, around 30. Could you tell us something about that person?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: The list says unknown, but since Sadika Redzep is with him, I think that he is from Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the fact that he had a military yellow belt and military socks have any significance?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have Brko Abdulah from Visegrad. He was probably a refugee in that area. Could you tell us where he was located, where he was based? All these people are from Nadioci. Can you say something about that, Mehmed Brko, number 38?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thirty-nine, you have a correction there. Have you these corrections in your notes? Is this person from Nadioci or from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Nadioci, Nadioci, which is the next village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forty, Paco Fehim. He was also a refugee. Was he based in Nadioci or in Ahmici, 40, number 40?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: A refugee from Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. But did he live in Ahmici or Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forty-one, again an unknown male. Can you say something more about that body?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I have nothing. My number is 19.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know whether he's from Ahmici or somewhere else. Then we have 42, this is a woman from -- the list says that she's from Nadioci. Can you confirm it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then 43 and 44, two charred bodies, males, two males. Can you tell us whether they are from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Ahmici-Santici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Because my notes say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are the grounds for your conclusion? It is not enough -- this is black, you can say white.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: The people who were working during the burial, they knew where these people came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about 43 and 44.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Sorry. This is my number 50. I don't have any information on these.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they from Ahmici or from some other village?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know? When I ask you something, you have to say "Yes" or "No" clearly so that it can be recorded. Let us go on. Then we come to 45 in the list, again an unknown male. The question is once again whether you know if he comes from Ahmici or from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I don't know. How am I supposed to say that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, was his body found in Ahmici or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: How could I know if I was in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you don't know, you can say it.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Sometimes you can know by the name and the surname where he comes from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not know where this corpse under 45 came from. Listen, I'm not trying to pull your leg. I'm simply trying to establish how many bodies came from Ahmici. So 46 is again an unknown man from Putis and one could deduce from this that number 46 is not from Ahmici, do we agree?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Because I cannot answer such questions. I was in Stari Vitez and I really cannot make any guesses or arbitrarily decide this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are checking his list and facts in his list, so will you please ask the witness to answer my questions? I think that I am being very polite and simply asking questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic is right. I mean, try to answer his questions, simply whether those people are from Ahmici, according to your notes.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: We compiled the list. When we knew that a person came from Ahmici, we stated so. Where we did not, I really cannot arbitrarily say "Yes" or "No".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But this list or whatever you call it is not something written by you but on the basis of your notes, and we simply have to see if this list, which is compiled by third persons, not you who took notes, did it in agreement with what you had noted down.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No. We evidently do not understand one another. In my notes, I have the numbers from the list that I was given by the HVO, from 1 to 103. And in these same HVO records under, shall we say 12, we have a Croat, Vlado Topalovic, he was not brought to us. And 39, it again says a Croat, so he wasn't brought to us. Ninety-seven, a Croat. Ninety-eight, a Croat. I have the HVO records. You still do not understand what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not identify any dead bodies. You said you did.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: You can see me on this monitor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why can't I ask you about those persons who are Muslims, and who figure on this list. If it doesn't say where these people come from, why couldn't I ask you where these people came from, whether from Ahmici or some other places? Does the record say that they come from Ahmici? There are persons where we have only the name and the last name and possibly the year of birth.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Because at that time we did not know whether they came from Ahmici or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you if you know it now?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No, because on the 10th of April, 1994, I left the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Before we go on. May I say that it probably would be very simple to ask the witness to give us his notebook so we make a photocopy and the photocopy could be given to the Defence counsel and then he can check on this list, if the witness does not mind handing the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why? I have nothing against having it photocopied. I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I shall be asking you two more questions, of course after the Prosecution has made their comments, but my questions will not be in the same manner as before. I will ask you about two more names which have nothing to do with this list, they have to do with something else. I believe my learned friend for the Prosecution was going to say something, so perhaps we shall wait for him?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, you are using the HVO list as your principal document?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So here we talked a great deal about whether there were any casualties among Muslim soldiers and we then said that there were no casualties among Muslim soldiers. Will you please then look at what it says by the number 47, by the victim under 47?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: This is 47 in the list --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Forty-seven in the list, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Not in the HVO list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your list?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am looking at that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sixty-nine on the HVO list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have the HVO list. I don't have the HVO list. So I need to read number 47.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please do it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, but which record? Which list?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The list that was given you today by the Prosecutor and from the Bosnian text, not the English text, from the Bosnian text in Bosnian language, will you tell us what does it say about the dead body under number 47?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: NN, male, aged about 30, brought in under number 69 of the HVO records of the 23rd April, '93. The record says: male, 30 years of age, 180 centimetres tall, weighing 68 kilograms, hair black and curly, camouflage uniform, military pullover, belt, and rubber boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And what does it say then under 54, the body under 54?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: NN male, about 35 years of age, brought under number 67 of the HVO records on the 23rd of April, 1993. The record says: male, 35 years, brown hair, camouflage uniform, 177 centimetres, military socks, boots with laces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted simply to hear you say that he was wearing complete military outfit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic? Cross-examined by Mr. Pavkovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rehibic, my name is Petar Pavkovic and I am counsel for the Defence. I should like to clarify once and for all this list that we were discussing, that we talked about here, and you already gave some explanations. Can we take it that this list of the 18th of March, 1994, was compiled on the basis of your and other people's notes made during the burial?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: On the basis of my notes, no. No, my notes were not used for it. It was done on the basis of the notes of an inspector of the crime department, that is those who examined the bodies and identified the bodies, and that service is headed by Ramo Vatric, and he was made responsible -- he was in charge of taking notes and making the list, and I did it just for my own sake, so I did it, this list of dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today we saw the Prosecution Exhibit 312 and in the forefront we saw a list of names on a placard, on a panel which was a memorial plaque or something like that, a commemorating table and we could see the names of various persons, and today you gave us some clarifications. So could you please tell us, if you know, who did this panel with those names and when was that done?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No, I can't, because I don't know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take the list which is before you, and on page 2, under 18, read out what it says -- this has been added in ballpoint pen.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Muzafer Puscul.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what does it say regarding number 23?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Sabahudin Mrkohja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about 25?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: You want me to answer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you. Tell me.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Samija Mrkohja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under 39?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Halib Pehlivanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forty-two?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Sadika Pehlivanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fifty-six?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Hajra, I guess, Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: This list I took from -- from the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know either how they came up with these names?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No, that is not quite true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you then explain to the Court how was it that he came up with those names?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Under 18, on the basis of the description, the age, features, trades, profession, place of birth, job, and that is how he was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes -- no, let's wait. Who established it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: The commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which commission?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Well, in this particular case, the three of us. At that time, after the burial, perhaps a couple of days later. In a conversation -- you see, Vitez is small. We knew people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was on the commission?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Ramo Vatres, then the cameraman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So immediately after the burial, you established that.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Well, we're talking about it, and on the basis of facts, we assumed which persons could be in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said that Ramo Vatres made a list, and that it was on the basis of his list that this list was made. So how then did it come to pass that subsequently, at a later date, this list be supplemented with the name of Muzafer Puscul in ballpoint because they didn't have specific facts as to who that individual was?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, and the memorial plaque at the cemetery still has the original names, that is the names as were established on the first day. No changes are made unless they're 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this list was done a year later on the 18th of March, 1994. 1994. So you said, on the basis of the list compiled by this Vatres, could you please explain then how is it that these -- that this information about the person under 18 were not included immediately? Here he was described as an unknown man, it said NN man, and then it was added in ballpoint that it was Muzafer Puscul?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Well, I told you that on the 24th of April, 1990 (sic), I left Stari Vitez. The command was submitted the original list of the first day when the bodies were received. Nothing could be changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, we can then conclude that you do not know how this information was added.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: We evidently are talking at cross-purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, we are not. I mean, I don't know what you don't understand because it is important to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: This is something that is very interesting. To this day, information is collected so as to establish their identity, to have data which shall be valid and true, so there may be some error. Until it is amended, until it is rectified on the panel, on that memorial plaque, then it's --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think that what it says on the panel, that is the thing which is trustworthy?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why did it then say that the NN male person under 18 is Muzafer Puscul, even on the panel?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Because the number of the body, the body buried under that number in that grave, and the information that we have, we assume, and on the basis of the description that went along with the body, that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I shall nevertheless go back to what you just said. Immediately, that is, those two or three days when you said after the burial, the three of you went through your notes, and on the basis of the descriptions in those notes, you arrived at the conclusion that it was Muzafer Puscul.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All these notes you submitted to whatever authority and, a year later, this list was drawn up. Why is it then that we do not have a Muzafer Puscul written in this list and instead have an unknown male?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I have just said that to the relevant commander we submitted the original list from the burial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you cannot really explain who was Muzafer Puscul in ballpoint above number 18?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: You want me to ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how do you know that that person NN, unknown man under 18, is Muzafer Puscul?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: On the basis of information that goes along with this identity. There is no other man in Vitez. But in this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how could you confirm that here, on this panel, under 18, is the same person?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Because it corresponds with the information that came with the body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. This was added. Wouldn't you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you see the same thing as I do, that something was added, that this was written additionally. And that would be --

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was, and there would be many things that would be added to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but it was added a year later. It wasn't added before 18th of March, 1994. It was added afterwards. And there would be even further additions. Thank you very much. I don't think we can manage this. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I do not have many questions. Cross-examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But let us look at these corrections, these amendments to the list. Will you please look at 25? Twenty-five, would you please read it, 25?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: With or without the correction?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Unknown man, charred, brought to cemetery under number 62 of the HVO record of the 22nd of April, 1993. The record reads: male charred body found in the house of Mustafa Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does it say above? What is the name above?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Samir Mrkohja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But a moment ago you said it was Samir. You said a husband and a wife? Didn't you say that? That's why we looked at it. You said that it was Sabahudin Mrkohja and his wife?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No, it's Samir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Samir. So what's the relationship between them? You said they were a couple, husband and wife, so how do you know that they were together in the same house?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Ahmic, Mustafa Ahmic, had a sister married in Ojice in the Sava valley and also married from Karaula, they were refugees in his home, and they were staying in that house, and hence the assumption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Perhaps you -- it was a slip of the tongue on your part and you said they were husband and wife, and we didn't realise how could they be. Besides, this is a list of people who were -- who died in Vitez and in places around Vitez on the 16th; is that so?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no other list, there are no other mass graves, there are no errors -- rather, there were no errors in the procedure, that is, those are people who died in Vitez and surroundings on the 16th; isn't that so? And that is the number established by the Muslim side, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: That is the number which was brought to Stari Vitez. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no other mass grave in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This number from 99 -- of 99 is, in fact, the definitive figure after Sakib Ahmic's family and Tahir Rogohjic were then buried there at a later date and this completes the list; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it also says that he was killed later?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You put, Ms. Glumac, the definitive figure. You mean the definitive figure for these graves or this grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, for this grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in -- that is 94 of them were buried on the 28th and subsequently five persons more were buried there?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. As for other casualties in Vitez, you don't think there are any, you don't know about other graves. We are talking about the 16th.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Moskowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Your Honour, if I may? Re-examined by Mr. Moskowitz:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify things, Mr. Rehibic. Essentially this list before us is the list of names and identities that you received from the HVO when you received that package, or those trucks full of corpses. These were compiled by the HVO and you just simply transferred them to another list with different numbers so you could identify where those bodies were buried in the ground; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these identifications were really made by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: All that is written here, yes, those identified persons, that was written by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After receiving that list and those bodies, further attempts were made to provide additional identification for unknown bodies in order to provide some closure for the family members; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Well, that is an ongoing task, to this day. Information is gathered so that NN, that is unknown persons, could be identified, attached a name on the basis of information or facts available, where they lived and various information collected in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's an unfinished task. The job continues to try to identify the people that were buried there?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite. It is a job which still goes on. It is something that continues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so let's look at number 18. Again, you had received certain information about this particular corpse. In addition to the fact that it was an unknown male, you received other information, including some information from an Ante Covic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, about some people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically about number 18.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Ante Covic says that the victim came from Kakanj because the notes, the records, are known, and that he was a technician and that he worked for Impregnacija and that he was the son-in-law of Sakib Ahmic. And on the basis of this information, I think I can affirm with certainty that the casualty, that the victim is Muzafer Puscul.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's a simple matter of putting two and two together and coming up with four; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about number 33, and I wanted to draw your attention to that for a moment. Take a look at number 33 and the information you received about where those bodies were found. Does it indicate where -- not in what village but in front of what home or structure?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: The record says under 33, NN male, charred, brought under number 44 of the HVO record of the 21st of April, 1993. Found in Mujo Dedic's shed. And the record says in Mujo Dedic's shed, found three charred bodies: a male charred corpse, male charred person, and male charred body, all three without any signs of identity and no other information, and each one of them had their number under which they were brought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know where Mujo Dedic's shed is located?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Well, really. Ahmici. No, not really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would depend on where Mujo Dedic's shed was located for you to determine where, in fact, these bodies were found; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Mujo Dedic -- yes, he lives in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that for a fact, that he lives in Ahmici, Mujo Dedic, or lived?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: It's a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked about two bodies that appeared to be dressed in a uniform, or in uniforms, and if I recall correctly in your direct testimony you stated that there were a couple of bodies found with uniforms on. Let's look at those two, number 47.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: And 54, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 54.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your list, which is based on the HVO identification list, does your list indicate in which village either of these two bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: According to the information which is in the notes, which is in the list, no, we don't see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting you. I should merely like to draw to your attention that in the case of these unknown men under 47, it is added in handwriting (redacted), that is (redacted), but my learned friend is following the English text so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so that was an indication of an attempt to continue to identify bodies so that the relatives could know where they were and who they were?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to 47, do you know where you obtained that information to identify that body?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: This information I learnt from talking to people. From their description, it was deduced that this was so and so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to identify number 54?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: At that point, when I was in Vitez, I couldn't. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked as to whether this was a complete list as to all bodies found. Is there a listing in this list for Fata Ahmic -- excuse me, Fata Pezer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the problem is that we can't answer this question because there are unknown persons marked as NN. This can be identified only by the family. We can't say that -- she is not on the list since we have NN, "unknown." The witness can't answer this question. The Prosecution could have established it through other means and ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. You're right. On the other hand, I think Mr. Moskowitz simply asked whether this name was on the list. I agree with you that it may not be on the list and still be covered by NN.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: The body may be there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The body may be there but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: -- but the name, is the question. Is the name there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But I think Counsel Slokovic-Glumac is right in saying that this is not decisive, because although the name may not be there, the body is probably in the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: But I might add that as we've had testimony that the whereabouts of this person is unknown to the relatives, it is probative to point out that, in fact, that is true. Her identity is unknown. Whether she is, in fact, buried in Stari Vitez or somewhere else, the family does not know where she is. She is not on this list, and therefore, they have no idea where she is.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: She is not on the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to clarify one last thing. This list does not contain, as far as you know, does it, the entire list of people who were killed in Ahmici on April 16, 1993, does it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It doesn't contain all the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask the witness to clarify one or two points about his notebook. I understand this is your notebook where you copied from the HVO list the various entries.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: This -- I didn't copy the notes, I -- in my notebook --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The HVO list, you had the HVO list, and I thought you said that you prepared a list in your own notebook on the basis of that HVO list, identification list, according to -- and also the numbering took up the numbering of the HVO list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. If you permit me? Your Honours, let me explain. In my notebook, I didn't write the data on the identification, I just wrote the first and last names and the number which tallies with the numbers of the HVO list, and on the HVO list, from 1 to 5, we have nothing. There is nothing, just the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. No other data. Number 6, the H -- Zlotrg Nedim. On the H -- Zlotrg Mira, 7. Varupa Midhat, 8. Tunovic Arifa, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Then tell me, what have you got on that list under number 53? Could you read what is next to number 53?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Under number 53, we just had the ordinal number 53, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And what about number 67?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Under number 67, NN, "unknown," that is, without any description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Number 69?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Sixty-nine. It said Pjanic Muamer, Muamer Pjanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I think what's happening, Your Honour, he's got a list by number of HVO, and it's a different numbering than the list you have in front of you. The numbering system was changed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Because I have under 47 of the list, typewritten list, brought as number 69 on the HVO list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So I'm asking, what is under 69 on the HVO list?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REHIBIC
utterances.text: Number 69, HVO, is Muamer Pjanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So it does not match because here, under 47 in the typewritten list, we have unknown male aged about 30. So I think it's important now for the witness to hand over his notebook to the registry so that maybe, with the assistance of the Prosecution and the Defence, photocopies -- I mean, to identify the various relevant pages, photocopies are made. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Relating to this, we do have the list and we will submit it as evidence, and that's why we should compare all the documents. This was the list made by the civilian defence when the bodies were collected. We should see what the witness has, what the list of ours is, how they compare, in order to determine the localities, the sites where the bodies were found. This is indispensable, therefore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I see that the Prosecution is agreeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I would only ask, to preserve his privacy with regard to his notebook, that only those pages that we need in order to verify this list be actually copied and distributed. I think the notebook has other things in that, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. But the witness maybe would be so kind as to indicate the relevant pages, the pages covering the list of the HVO list, and then he will show his notebook to the registry, but I think probably one person from each side should be present, without, of course, being too inquisitive, looking into matters which may be covered by privacy, but he should -- I think that the witness does not mind. It would be of great importance for the Court to have that list - I am referring to the HVO list - to make comparisons with the list which the Defence is going to produce. Also, because as I said, we have just come across an inconsistency.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I also note that there appear to be more than one HVO list from different dates, April 23rd, April 20th, April 24th. So that is also another bit of a mystery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you permit me, Your Honours, I would add an explanation? It is correct that there are contradictions and inconsistencies. On page 68 of the HVO record, Ibrahim Karic. It says Ibrahim Karic. He is alive. In another case we have a living person, number 42, Amir Ahmic. He is alive. And the record listed him as dead. That's why the HVO number 103 -- and we received only 96 bodies. And that's the reason for the difference in the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I think there is no objection to the witness being released? Thank you, Mr. Rehibic, for testifying. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The notebook, if you don't mind giving the notebook to the ... We can break now for tea or coffee and maybe resume in fifteen minutes? Twenty minutes. Twenty minutes. So we can start with your next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Moskowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, to inform the Court, the relevant parts of the notes have been copied or are in the process now of being copied, and it occurred, I think, both to me and to Defence counsel that it might be useful to have that witness go over his notes with the Court and explain what is in those notes because it's not, I think, immediately apparent what those notes mean and where that information came from, but, of course, I would leave that up to the Court's discretion, if the Court thinks that is a good idea, and perhaps turn to Defence counsel to see if they think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel Pavkovic? May I suggest that then we give the Defence counsel some time so we could ask the witness to come back tomorrow morning so that you have the evening to go through the various notes and we go on with the next witness. When he comes back, of course, I think this will not take too much time. This must be a matter of a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wanted to ask something else. The Defence has -- it is not clear to the Defence whether the Prosecutor -- whether this has been entered into the evidence. This is the document of the 18th of March, 1994, number 307. We don't know whether this has been accepted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: It has been offered into evidence and I think accepted into evidence, unless there is a reconsideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No. I thought there was no objection from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, true, but later, in the examination of the witness, we saw that the witness couldn't say who wrote it and when he wrote it in ballpoint over 23, 25, et cetera, and 56, and therefore, in that part, the Defence thinks that we cannot accept the content of the document as evidence, as part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Why? You may not accept the -- I mean, the handwriting, that somebody put in a few names, pencilled in a few names, but the exhibit as such I think it's acceptable, can be admitted, subject to your reservations concerning those particular names. I agree with you that we don't know who wrote in those names, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course we don't know who wrote it, nor when he wrote it. It is essential that you saw from the examination that the Prosecution pays great attention to that. We want to point out that this cannot be admitted. Furthermore, what is written in ballpoint was done only in the Bosnian version, that is, in the original, and not in the English transcript. This is another reason why we shouldn't admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. It is admitted into evidence and we will take into account, of course, your reservations. It is not the final list and, in the end, we will verify, compare the various lists, and we will make a finding. So it is admitted into evidence, both 307 and 307A, and, of course, we are aware that on 307A, the hand-written names are not reproduced, and we will come back later on to this matter of the notes taken by the witness in his notebook. Do you agree that we should move on to our next witness and maybe tomorrow morning we will come back to the present witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could you please stand and would you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Moskowitz:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we begin by having you give us your name and your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Edib Zlotrg, born on the 21st of October, 1953.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zlotrg, could you tell us what your profession is?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I'm a criminal technician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you perform that job?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: At the police station at Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Since 1974.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did your relationship with Vlado Santic begin? How did you begin to know each other?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: When he came to my street in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were, in fact, neighbours or you began to become acquainted as neighbours in 1974?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you continue that relationship with Vlado Santic up until 1993, and even beyond?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you characterise your friendship with Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: We were friends. We visited each other's houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you close friends?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you see each other over the years?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1979, did you and Vlado Santic move into a different apartment building?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how your apartments were situated?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: We lived in Marsala Tita Street, 82. Mr. Santic's apartment was number 41, and mine, 42. He lived in a one-room apartment and myself in a three-room flat, next door to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your family and the Santic family socialise?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. We drank coffee together. We had coffee together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do anything else together? Did you see each other on a frequent occasion?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. Soon after that, we worked together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in 1984 and 1985, did Vlado Santic move again?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He moved to the building next door -- to the next house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what else was located in that building next door?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: A chess club.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Vlado Santic moved to another building, did you continue to speak to him and socialise with Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes, we were together at work too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of work did Vlado Santic do at that time?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: He was assistant commander of the police station and he later worked as inspector in the criminal department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you join the police department?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your function or duties in 1986 when you joined the police department?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I was the head of the materials and equipment department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what point did you become a criminal technician, or forensic technician?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
