utterances.text: Was this -- were you assigned to the same police department as Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. We shared the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would see each other and work with each other every day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at that time, when you knew him back in the 1980s and the early 1990s, how would you characterise Vlado Santic's work as a police officer and as an inspector?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: He was conscientious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he follow the rules pretty well?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want to direct your attention to May of 1992, and specifically to the killing of a person called Trako Samir. Do you remember that case?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Trako Samir killed?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: According to colleagues who did the first investigation, in the hotel, in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was in charge of that investigation; do you know?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Vladimir Santic, and I was to be there as the technician on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the investigation of the killing of Trako Samir at the Hotel Vitez carried out according to the rules of procedure as you understood them back then?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened? Why wasn't it? I mean, what was not done or what was done that should not have been done?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Under the orders of the then commander of the police station, Mr. Skopljak, Frano Sucic as the forensic technician was called in instead of me, and Vlado Santic and Frano Sucic did the on-site investigation without the presence of the judge and the prosecutor. We went to see the scene of the crime only the next day when the judge from Travnik came -- I can't remember his name, and there were also present Santic and Sucic and Mr. Fran Pihjo represented the army and Salem Topcic and myself. The scene of the crime had been tampered with, the hotel had been cleaned, there were no other traces of blood, of anything, when we arrived in the morning, so that we could not really do what was necessary, although Mr. Santic was well aware that the place had to be ensured secured until the arrival of the judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the victim of this murder, Trako Samir, what ethnic group did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone ever, as far as you know, arrested or prosecuted for that crime?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time period, did you notice whether Vlado Santic took to wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: On several occasions, he came to work wearing the HVO uniform, the camouflage one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know it was an HVO uniform?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: He had the insignia on his sleeve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: HVO patch?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Pero Skopljak. Did you notice whether, while you were at the police station during those days, whether there was some kind of relationship between Pero Skopljak and Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. Vlado Santic was the confidant of Pero Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was Pero Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: The head of the station, that is, of the police station at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what political party was he?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to direct your attention to a little later in the year of '92, the 20th of November, 1992. Do you recall being arrested on that day?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us very briefly what the circumstances of that arrest were?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: The night before that, two members of the army were killed on the road to Kruscica, and because of the situation in the field, we had agreed with the command of the Military Police, of the brigade police, Marijan Jukic and the head of the civilian criminal investigation police of HZ, that is Herceg-Bosna, that is Miro Lazarovic, having also consulted the military judge and the military prosecutor in Zenica, not to do the investigation on site that night but to postpone it for the 20th of November, 9.00 in the morning. On the 20th of November, at 9.00 in the morning, I waited for the investigating team from Zenica to arrive. I was waiting for them in front of the police station in Vitez, and on that occasion, Poljskic Enes, the inspector from Zenica and I went to the Territorial Defence headquarters to get the particulars for those two people, that is killed and severely wounded members of the army. There we were -- driver of the official vehicle of the Territorial Defence staff, and we were also accompanied by Ramo Vatres, the inspector of the criminal investigation -- Military Police, that is department of the army of B and H, and in front of the hotel by the petrol station we were stopped by the Military Police of the Croatian Defence Council who forced us to get out of the car. When I tried to explain to a policeman that we are on this investigation team, it all had been agreed with his superiors to let us through, he uncocked his rifle and with his butt he pushed me towards the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be the Hotel Vitez that you went to?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The Hotel Vitez, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, were you in a uniform at that time?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: No, none of us was wearing a uniform with the exception of the driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened at the Hotel Vitez when you were taken there under arrest?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: When they brought us into the hotel, they left us in the passage, in the corridor, and we had to wait. And after a while, Mr. Santic came out wearing a camouflage uniform, and when the inspector of the Military Police from the criminal investigation of the Military Police in Zenica asked what was the matter, he said he did not know, and then I said that we were a part of the investigation team and that up there in the field, the judge and the rest of the team were waiting for us so that we could proceed with the investigation. Vlado said he was going to see about what he could do. Some 15 or 20 minutes later, he returned, returned the pistol to Enes Poljskic, gave us the keys and told us we were free to go. And the military policeman then saw us to the official vehicle of the B and H army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on what you saw that day at the Hotel Vitez, who was in charge of the Military Police officers that had you under arrest that day?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I do not know who was in charge, but since the policemen were carrying out the orders of Vlado Santic, I guess I should assume that he was in some position of command, but what he was doing, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequent to that, did you receive information about the position that Vlado Santic had with respect to the Military Police?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. I learned that he was the commander of a Military Police unit, regional Military Police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which company he commanded?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I didn't know then. Subsequently I did learn that it was Company 1 of the 4th regiment because they were the only ones who were stationed in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come to know where this 1st Company was stationed specifically, in what building?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: One platoon was in the Bungalow in Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want to draw your attention to the first part of 1993, and specifically again to the case involving Mr. Salkic. Do you remember that investigation?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. It was in early February 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you respond to the scene of that crime?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the scene of the crime?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: In Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see when you arrived at the scene, and what did you learn?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: When we arrived at the scene, that is, the investigation team, the investigating team of the Military Police of the Croatian Defence Council was leaving the site, and my colleague, Ilija Marjanovic told me on that occasion that the murder had been committed by Cicko and that he was in the military prison. I don't remember if he mentioned Kaonik or something else. When we arrived at the site, we only found blood in the passage near the entrance door, and in the living room, on the couch, there was Salkic's body, and it was beheaded and a part of the neck was missing. On the opposite wall, the wall opposite to the entrance door had all been destroyed by an explosion and the roof had caved in, and there were bloodstains all over the walls and the ceiling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you interview any eyewitnesses to the crime, and if so, what did you learn about how this happened?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: During the night hours, Cicko came to the door of the house belonging to the Salkic family, and when Esad opened the door, according to eyewitnesses, he fired three shots from the rifle, aiming at the chest, and Esad Salkic must have died on the spot from these wounds. Near the door at this place we found bloodstains. Then eyewitnesses said that Cicko had carried it into the living room and put him on the couch and that after that, he mined the house, and due to the mine, the house was demolished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who Cicko is?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Miroslav Bralo, nicknamed Cicko, member of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you indicated that the investigators from the HVO told you that Mr. Bralo had been arrested for this crime, and you didn't know the name of the gaol that he was taken to, but could you tell us whether this was a civil gaol or Military Police gaol that he was taken to, as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Military Police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you come to learn from any of these eyewitnesses how the body of Mr. Salkic was mutilated? I believe you indicated that the head was missing and part of the neck.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Nobody saw that, and it is very likely that it happened due to the explosion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want to draw your attention to April 26, 1993. This is days after the attacks in the Lasva Valley. Were you arrested at that time and, if so, where were you placed?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the cinema hall in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that day, were you taken somewhere?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. That night, Zlatko Nakic, a member of the Military Police of the Croatian Defence Council, sometime around 10.00 or 11.00 in the evening, woke we up and took me out into the lobby of the cinema, and we were about ten of us, and a list was made of our names. They then took us to the Bungalow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you taken to the Bungalow?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: In a van, TAM, a closed one, a closed van, T-A-M van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see outside as you were driving towards the Bungalow?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when you arrived at the Bungalow?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: We reached the parking lot of the Bungalow, then the driver and assistant driver ordered us to get out of the van, to put our hands up behind our heads, to turn -- to face the van and to squat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you forced to hold that position, squatting near the van?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: About an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close were you to the Bungalow while you were squatting next to the van?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Some 10 metres perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were in that position near the Bungalow, did you hear any voices you recognised?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose voice did you hear?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Vladimir Santic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over what period of time did you hear that voice?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: It could have been sometime between 10.30 until 12.30, perhaps a little later, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown P119, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at this photograph which is 119, Exhibit 119, and tell us what that shows?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: It has the building of the Bungalow and it is taken from the road, from road E5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this picture show an area where you were that day on April 26 when you heard the voice of Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take the pointer next to you and -- don't point on the TV monitor but point on the picture -- show us where you recall being when you were listening to that voice.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Between the Bungalow and this van here, a little higher up, to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were in that position and listening to Vlado Santic's voice, did you hear his voice witness or more than once?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: More than once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you be sure that was the voice of Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I know him very well indeed and I couldn't be mistaken about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any doubt in your mind that that was the voice of your old friend, Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken after that; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: That night they took us to Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you supposed to do or required to do at Kaonik or in the area of Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: We only spent the night there, not in the military prison but in the hangar which was above the military prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the next day, where were you taken and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: The next day, they took us to the area of Kratine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: We dug trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of that operation?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Miroslav Bralo, Cicko, was the commander in the area of responsibility of -- that is the area of Kratine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Miroslav Bralo in Kratine while you were digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes, I did, several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same Miroslav Bralo who you had been told had been sent to gaol for the killing of Mr. Salkic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, did you see any soldiers with any kind of communication devices?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. Members of the Military Police used to come up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of communication devices did you see them with?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Well, they had Motorolas, but the make, I don't know which make it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point, could you overhear anybody speaking on one of those Motorolas or walkie-talkies?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear when they communicated with Mr. Santic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "when they communicated with Mr. Santic." How do you know they were communicating with Mr. Santic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Because I know him very well and I've heard his voice over various means of communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear his voice on that occasion on the walkie-talkie?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what the occasion was that required communication with Mr. Santic on a walkie-talkie? What had been going on at Kratine?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: They contacted Vladimir Santic to get further orders, to get instructions for work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Cicko was in charge. Did he threaten you in any way?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you recall about that?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: He first made some ten of us make the sign of the cross, and a gypsy could not do it properly and then Cicko took an axe and came with it above his head, turned the blunt side of the axe and told him that unless he made the proper sign of a cross, that he would kill him. And then this Romany fortunately managed to make the proper sign of the cross, and Cicko then made him repeat it ten times, evidently in the hope that he would make a mistake and so that he would kill him, but he always made the sign of the cross properly. Then he told us, if any one of us escaped, that he would kill us all. So that one time, one of us was digging a trench a little bit further away, and at twilight, when they brought us to that house where his headquarters were, that fellow was missing, and he told us, unless he turns up within an hour, that he would liquidate us all. However, they brought in this fellow meanwhile. On a third occasion, when we had just finished digging and we evidently became a burden to him because he had to feed us and there was nothing for us to do, then he said he would liquidate us all unless somebody came from the Bungalow and took us back. But shortly afterwards, three or four members of the HVO in black uniforms arrived and they communicated with Vlado Santic to ask him what to do with us. Then over the walkie-talkie they said, repeatedly said, that they would kill us unless they sent a vehicle to fetch us because we had -- they didn't know what to use us for up there anymore. And only around 10.00 or half past 10.00 in the evening they agreed that a vehicle would come to fetch us. So that is how we stayed alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were then taken back to the cinema that night?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, ultimately, you were released, were you not?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes, on the 30th of April, when Mr. Petkovic and Sefer Halilovic agreed that all for all would be released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you were re-arrested again and then released again after that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: They didn't catch me. I didn't flee anywhere. I was in my flat. I had nowhere to go. The next day, the very next day, on the 1st of May, Ante Covic came, a member of the HVO Military Police together with another policeman, whose name I don't remember, and they told my wife they were taking me to make a statement and that I would return immediately, but I stayed in the cinema at Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a prisoner, did you spend some time at the chess club?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. A day or two later, in the cinema hall, in the morning, around 2.00 or 3.00, of the 30 of us in the hall, they singled out two or three. They took us out to the hall and then they brought other prisoners who were in other camps in Vitez, in the town of Vitez. So that that night, there were 12 of us there, a total of 12. We were taken in a van to the chess club premises. The next day, 13 more persons were brought. In the end, we were 13 there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the chess club was being used as a kind of prison at that time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes, a hidden prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A hidden prison. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: They hid the 13 of us. What they wanted to do with us, I don't know, because it had been agreed that all prisoners would be released. However, we got the list -- we managed to send the list to the prisoners in the hall. On the 5th of May -- I'm not quite sure about that date -- when the UNPROFOR and Red Cross representatives came to the cinema hall to monitor the release of all the prisoners, then our people gave them the list and said that 13 persons were missing. That was us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. Are all these details relevant to our case? I wonder whether we need to go into all these details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: We can move quickly to the last point I'm going to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving now to the last point. You were ultimately released from the chess club; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were ultimately released from captivity at sometime in May or June; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: In May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know a man by the name of Ivan Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is he?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: He is a lawyer. He was a judge at the District Court in Vitez. He worked in the police station. He later went to the Military Police, the regional Military Police as an inspector. He is Vlado Santic's wife's brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you run into Ivan Josipovic shortly after you were released in June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him shortly after my release after the Bosnian and Herzegovinan army captured him in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the circumstances under which you saw Mr. Josipovic, Ivan?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: I knew Ivan, and I went to see what he said, what he told our investigators. When I saw that they carried out the investigation contrary to facts, I said some things that I knew about him. We knew that the unit of the regional police was stationed at the Bungalow, in the Bungalow, and I asked him directly what Santic's role was in all this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Josipovic, the brother-in-law of Vlado Santic, tell you when you asked him that question?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: He said then that Santic was conducting the attack on Ahmici from the Bungalow direction, from the direction of the Bungalow. He was physically -- he was present in Ahmici. He was there in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour. Your Honour, I do have one more item I would like to take up with this witness, and if the usher could be so kind to provide the witness with this exhibit, and we have English translations and copies for the Court and Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 313, English translation 313A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: For information of the Court, and perhaps before I question this witness about this document, this is a document that we have received in the original form I believe today. We did receive a Xerox copy of this original earlier, a couple of days ago, when this witness came from Central Bosnia. This witness was not present at the meeting that this document commemorates, and it may not be possible for him to authenticate this document, so I will say that up front, but he can read the signatures and tell us who signed this document to the best of his ability; and we would hope, at a later date, to be able to authenticate the document in some way, but that may prove to be difficult except perhaps through handwriting samples as will be made, I think, clear when I ask this witness to provide some information about this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zlotrg, could you look at what has been marked 313 which is the original now of the document that you had provided to us earlier in a Xerox form? Now, this document, as you can see, talks about an agreement that took place in October 1992. Were you present when that agreement was reached in Ahmici in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: No. All the signatories, Muslims, of this agreement, are dead. They were killed on the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you, if you could, read for us the names of the signatories to this document, first starting on the left which says "For the HVO"?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: For the HVO, Santic Nenad, Livancic Zeljko, and Zoran Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the right-hand side, for the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: On the right, Muris Ahmic, Nazif Ahmic, Fahrudin Ahmic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you have any --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: -- and Islam Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to the whereabouts of the four signatories for the Muslim people on this document?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: They died on the 16th of April in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned Zoran Kupreskic. Which signature do you believe is, in fact, Zoran Kupreskic's signature?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: The last one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how you came to have possession of a Xerox copy of this document?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: From the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was as a result of a communiqué from the Office of the Prosecutor seeking documents or materials pertaining to this case; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in a bit of an awkward situation with regard to this document because we have received it so late in the case. It does appear that if these names are correct with regard to the Muslim signatories, that they are indeed not alive to testify about this agreement. I note that the signature that is allegedly the signature of Zoran Kupreskic appears to be simply "Zoran."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Zlotrg, that we're looking at a signature that simply says "Zoran"?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG
utterances.text: Yes, that's what is written, but people who worked with Zoran told me that it was his signature and also the -- that the meeting was held and that seven persons were present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: It may be necessary, since now we do have the original, to request a handwriting sample from Mr. Kupreskic, Zoran, to try to compare the signature and to try to establish its authenticity and its connection with the Defendant unless, of course, Zoran Kupreskic or his counsel will admit that this is, in fact, his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, regardless of how Zoran Kupreskic will defend himself in this case, it doesn't matter. The giving of the signature is help to the Defence (sic). I don't think he is obliged to help the Defence (sic) in any way and to give his signature because of the expertise, and this situation cannot be taken as evidence against him, that is, to prove any relationship. I think that he shouldn't participate in the process of establishing facts. It is not his duty to give -- he is under no obligation to give his signature. I think a decision, a ruling, was made by this Court that nobody is obliged to contribute to the Defence (sic) by his actions or with his actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: There was a misunderstanding. According to the translation, you said "nobody is obliged to contribute to the Defence by his actions." You mean the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So you are talking on behalf of Mr. Zoran Kupreskic. I wonder whether Mr. Radovic agrees with you because I think Mr. Radovic, you are counsel for --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I agree. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. We will decide on this and we will make a ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. At this point we would offer this only for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. So it's 313 and 313A for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will make a ruling on this matter, but I wonder whether we could go on with cross-examination. We might finish this afternoon. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can go on. I don't know whether you intend to prolong the hearing, but I don't think I can finish in ten minutes. In any case, it would be more convenient for me if we went on tomorrow. In any case, I will follow what you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. You may start and we will go on until 5.15, so you have 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, before I start questioning the witness, it might be useful for us to get some information from the Prosecution because all that the witness stated today or almost everything, I hear and my colleagues, Defence counsel, hear for the first time. The Prosecutor submitted to the Defence the statement of the witness made on the 10th of June, 1997. At the end of that statement, it says that the witness made some notes for himself on all the events that took place and on other events in the area of the municipality of Vitez from 1991 until 1993, and these notes he considers, as stated here, as part of his interview. It states further that these notes are enclosed -- are enclosed. Ten pages of the notes. The Defence never received these notes. In view of this fact then, I submit to the Court that the Prosecution should state what happened to the notes, and this would be the reason why I would like to think about my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You are right. We too received only this short statement of one page and a few lines, no notes, and I wonder whether Mr. Moskowitz can tell us about those notes, why they were not handed over to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate Defence counsel pointing that out because I had not noticed that there were notes attached and, in fact, I have no notes myself, so I am at a loss at this point to tell you where the notes are. They are not in my file, and I have never seen them before. You know, if it's appropriate to have these notes turned over to Defence counsel overnight for him to look at it for tomorrow, that would be fine with the Prosecution. We would not object to that. I frankly had not noticed that before, and I do not have the notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So you may try to find these notes right away and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, the witness may have them. I don't know if he brought them with him or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: So we will provide them tonight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Do you have the notes, the ten pages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: In what language? In Serbo-Croatian probably, Croatian, Bosniak? Not in English. Probably there is an English copy for the Prosecutor. Anyway, the original should be handed over right away to the Defence, and Defence counsel is right in saying that -- whatever was said this afternoon was new also to the Court. We had read, of course, carefully that statement that this was new, so therefore, you need time, and we will resume tomorrow at 9.30. Yes, Counsel? Yes, please. Do you want to say -- no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So you have more time if we resume at 9.30, but we would like to try to finish by tomorrow afternoon, so that on Friday at 10.00 we will have a meeting with the registry about the on-site visit at 9.00. At 10.00, we would start with the pre-Defence conference, which should take not more than one hour so that we can finish as soon as possible. In particular, Defence counsel may wish to go back to Zagreb or Sarajevo and prepare for the visit. Do you think we can finish -- let us try to finish by tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: We only have, as the Court knows, two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But one -- for one, we will need not more than twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Precisely. And the other one may not be that much longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Ten minutes. So tomorrow morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 4.55 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of October, 1998, at 9.30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
